elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to each Party's total aggregate liability.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 applies the cap to “each Party's total aggregate liability” and expressly states that the cap is mutual.

elements.element: The fee-based limb of the cap is fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 uses “fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim” as limb (a).

elements.element: The cap includes a USD 1,000,000 limb.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 specifies “USD 1,000,000” as limb (b).

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the 12-month fee-based limb and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 expressly caps liability at “the greater of” limbs (a) and (b).

elements.element: Indirect damages are mutually excluded.
elements.evidence: Section 21.2 states that “neither Party is liable for indirect” damages, subject to Excluded Claims and legal excludability.

elements.element: Consequential damages are mutually excluded.
elements.evidence: Section 21.2 states that “neither Party is liable for ... consequential damages,” subject to Excluded Claims and legal excludability.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Confidentiality breaches are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, and Section 21.1 does not apply to Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Breach of data-protection obligations is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Data-protection breaches are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, and Section 21.1 does not apply to Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Breach of security obligations is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Security breaches are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, and Section 21.1 does not apply to Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, and Section 21.1 does not apply to Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Gross negligence is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is an Excluded Claim under Section 21.3, and Section 21.1 does not apply to Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Wilful misconduct is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is an Excluded Claim under Section 21.3, and Section 21.1 does not apply to Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Fraud is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Fraud is an Excluded Claim under Section 21.3, and Section 21.1 does not apply to Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Infringement of the other Party's intellectual property is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 includes “infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property” as an Excluded Claim, which Section 21.1 leaves uncapped.

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not damages for cap purposes.
elements.evidence: Section 21.3 states that Customer's obligation to pay all amounts due is not damages and is not limited by the Section.

elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both Parties.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 applies to each Party and expressly states that the cap is mutual.

elements.element: The cap amount is 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered cap is the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, not a cap equal solely to 12 months' fees.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3 and therefore outside Section 21.1's cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Confidentiality breaches are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3 and therefore outside Section 21.1's cap.

elements.element: Gross negligence is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is an Excluded Claim under Section 21.3 and therefore outside Section 21.1's cap.

result.reason: The rendered language satisfies every preferred element, including the mutual greater-of cap, mutual damages exclusion, all required uncapped carve-outs, and the payment-obligation treatment. It does not independently satisfy the fallback because its actual cap is not equal solely to 12 months' fees. The changes are confined to implementing the preferred position and preserve the remaining liability allocation. Drafting quality is reduced because lowercase “fees” is not defined, despite the agreement retaining a defined and materially narrower uppercase “Fees” term; defining the intended fee base would avoid interpretive uncertainty. “All amounts due” is also broader and less precise than an express reference to Customer's contractual payment obligations.
